mechanism: At each MA-cross base signal, compute a large bank of standard oscillators (ADX, ATR, RSI, Stoch, MFI, MACD, StdDev, etc.) on every MT5 timeframe up to D1, sampling each buffer at bar shifts 1, 2, and 15 so the vector encodes both level and short-horizon dynamics; CatBoost then classifies whether the base signal is tradable.
data_needed: OHLC + tick/real volume; ~24 oscillator handles × all TFs × 3 shifts (~2000 buffers); binary target from subsequent MA-cross trade PnL after commission.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Si Splice (USDRUB_TOM futures splice), M1 OHLC simulation; base signal MA on M2; predictors through D1; train/test 2014-06–2019-ish, exam 2019-08–2020-10
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a multi-horizon oscillator state vector synchronized to an event (MA touch/cross) rather than a single-TF snapshot—usable as a dense sensing feature pack for regime-conditioned signal filters.
quote: I believe that in addition to the information that has formed by the current moment, the model should receive the information that describes the movement that lead to the current moment.

mechanism: Among predictor families, encode price vs significant levels (session open, regression channel, MAs) not only in fixed points/% of day open but also as percentage of a volatility level and relative to trend segments on different TFs—so distance-to-level is scaled by current vol regime.
data_needed: Price, level series, and a volatility measure (e.g. ATR/StdDev) on matching TFs; percent-of-vol distances.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Si Splice futures; multi-TF including M1–D1 oscillator/ATR family
why_new_for_mis: Explicit vol-normalized geometry-to-level sensors—MIS can compare structural distance across quiet vs expanded regimes without fixed-point thresholds.
quote: In a fixed range as a percentage: Relative to the day opening price or level; Relative to the volatility level; Relative to trend segments of different TFs

mechanism: Fit a Gaussian Mixture (n_components≈75, full covariance) on the joint feature+label space (MA-increment lookbacks), then sample synthetic examples from the posterior; this breaks loop autocorrelation and softens class overlap before CatBoost training, selecting models by OOS R².
data_needed: EURUSD H1 closes; features = close−MA for MA periods [15,55,150,250] over LOOK_BACK=5; random-horizon labels min–max bars with markup filter.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train ~2020, test back to 2015
why_new_for_mis: Treats training-sample geometry (autocorrelation/overlap) as a sensing/preconditioning problem—MIS can regenerate cleaner class-conditional clouds before fitting regime classifiers.
quote: GMM generates samples randomly, this leads to data pluralism. The best model can be selected using brute force.

mechanism: Diagnose naive sampling via residual autocorrelation: Model-1 residuals inherit neighboring-sample correlation tied to training-period volatility structure; target Model-2 with roughly constant residual variance so the learner covers more than train-vol-specific patterns.
data_needed: Labeled feature series; model residuals (Pearson residuals for classification); variance-stability check across time.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 feature/label construction as above
why_new_for_mis: Residual-variance / autocorrelation diagnostic as a volatility-regime overfit sensor on ML training sets—flags when a model only learned local vol texture.
quote: Model 1 has autocorrelation of residuals, which can be compared to model overfitting on certain market properties (for example, related to the volatility of training data)

mechanism: Splits MQL indicators/EAs into Model/View/Controller folders and classes for maintainability; no market-state sensing is proposed beyond a trivial (open+close)/2 line and a calendar pending-order EA.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic chart; multi-JPY pairs in sample EA (AUDJPY, CADJPY, EURJPY, …)
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing content after full read—software design pattern tutorial.
quote: the idea is to split an existing code into three separate components: Model, View and Controller.

mechanism: Bar-by-bar search for tops/bottoms as opposite run-length candle series (MinimumSeriesBarsM consecutive same-direction bodies), then select N extrema for Double/Triple/Head-Shoulders family; FormationDirection from which extremum type is closest to market.
data_needed: OHLC bars; MinimumSeriesBars; TopsM; arrays of Top structs with time/index/price.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MT5 visual tester examples (triple top shown); any symbol/TF supported by prototype
why_new_for_mis: Discrete multi-top/bottom structural regime sensor with quantitative shoulder balance—feeds reversal-regime flags without fractal-only logic.
quote: Without tops and bottoms, the whole pattern is meaningless, since the presence of tops and bottoms is a required condition for the pattern

mechanism: Build horizontal neck at min-low (tops) / max-high (bottoms) between extreme pattern pivots; require left-side full-bar cross of neck (prior trend), right-side close through neck at bar 0 for entry, and optimistic target distance matched by a preceding move (bWasTrend)—invalid if price escapes pattern bounds mid-path.
data_needed: Selected Tops/Bottoms; Neck line equation; FarestTop height; RelativeUnstability* filters; OptimistLine.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MT5 strategy-tester visualization of triple/double tops
why_new_for_mis: Actionable regime-change trigger: neck-break only when prior impulse ≥ pattern height—MIS change sensor with built-in false-pattern rejection.
quote: We need both detection and finding exactly at the point from which we can trade — where we can immediately open a position, knowing that we are at the entry point.

mechanism: Run CatBoost cross_val_predict on MA-increment features; mark bars where CV prediction ≠ label as bad; set meta_labels=0 on those indices. Train main model only on meta_labels==1 (direction) and a second meta-model on all rows to allow/deny trading—transfers hard cases to a tradeability gate.
data_needed: EURUSD H1 closes; PERIODS MA increments (e.g. 10–40); random-horizon labels+markup meta; folds_number, iter, depth, l_rate.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; BACKWARD 2015-01-01, FORWARD 2022-01-01; ONNX export to MT5
why_new_for_mis: Self-controlled predictability / causal-filter sensor: separates persistently classifiable states from associative noise—MIS neural gate for when direction models are trustworthy.
quote: by eliminating bad training examples, we will look for situations that, on average, bring profit. And we will try not to trade in places that, on average, cause losses.

mechanism: From three successive pivots draw median line (ML) through midpoint of [1]-[2]; parallels MLH form channel. ML slope = local trend; price at ML/MLH expected to bounce, gap, or slide; consecutive same-direction MLs mark strong trend regime; sliding parallels (SH) track breakouts that still follow main trend.
data_needed: Pivot highs/lows; Andrews pitchfork / ML+MLH geometry; optional warning lines at equal action-reaction distance.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY Monthly/Daily; EURUSD H1 examples throughout
why_new_for_mis: Geometric local-trend regime sensor from action-reaction pitchforks—slope, channel containment, and multi-ML concurrence as structured regime features.
quote: The first parameter this line has is the slope. If the line is sloping down, then the local trend is down, and vice versa

mechanism: If price fails to reach ML and breaks MLH against ML slope (Hagopian), treat as flat/correction regime; optionally draw trendline on the failed-attempt extrema and enter on its break—author notes this often marks consolidation before a powerful post-flat move.
data_needed: Pitchfork ML/MLH; price path vs ML; extrema of failed-attempt zone.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY Monthly examples of failed ML reaches
why_new_for_mis: Explicit failed-attraction → flat-regime sensor complementary to channel-trend—MIS can flag consolidation vs trending pitchfork states.
quote: this situation simply means that the price is in a flat zone (or in a correction if we use Elliott's terminology).

mechanism: After a sharp rise/fall, fan 10°–80° lines from the extremum; while price stays in steepest bands position can ride; cross of 20°→often 30°, stay inside 40° keeps trend; cross of 40° (esp. after another surge) signals likely sharp reversal—angle-band regime/change sensor (scale-dependent but empirically sticky).
data_needed: Pivot for fan origin; chart-scale-aware 10° ray set (attached Horn script); close relative to rays.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY Monthly and Daily horn examples; script for MQL4/MQL5
why_new_for_mis: Angular speed-regime ladder as a change sensor—maps trend strength decay into discrete angle bands rather than oscillator thresholds.
quote: If the price crosses the 40° line, a sharp trend reversal is likely to be expected.

mechanism: Train pure AR models (order search by SSE) on close or mid prices with optional differencing; save/load .model; Predict(1, pricebuffer) each new bar using GetMinModelInputs() history—integrate differenced forecasts back to price domain for a one-step sequence forecast sensor.
data_needed: Close or (H+L)/2 series; AR order, diff flag; min inputs = diff_order + max AR lag (+ MA lag×factor if MA terms).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUDUSD M1 example training window 2020–2021; indicator/EA apply saved model
why_new_for_mis: Native MQL ARIMA one-step temporal dependence sensor with explicit differencing/integration—lightweight sequence forecast feature without Python.
quote: Based on the next bar prediction we buy if the forecast close is larger than the last known close. And sell if the forecast is less.

mechanism: Require both 14- and 5-period Stochastics to hit OS/OB together, bounce, then retest OS/OB near-simultaneously while price is above (longs) or below (shorts) the 200-MA—MA side is the trend regime filter; Fib projections from the two touch extremes set targets.
data_needed: Two iStochastic handles; iMA 200; swing high/low between touches for Fib 61.8/100 projections.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Demo M30, shift=300, 2013–2023-06; notes poor performance in 2008–2014 and 2020 crisis
why_new_for_mis: Dual-momentum exhaustion retest gated by long MA regime—MIS regime+exhaustion composite rather than single-oscillator OB/OS.
quote: The whole process must be done while the market is above the 200-period moving average.

mechanism: Compute Heiken-Ashi OHLC (HA-close=(O+H+L+C)/4, HA-open=mid of prior HA, HA-H/L extremes) to smooth noise; treat HA close>open vs close<open color as bullish/bearish regime and fire on color flip (optionally require MA cross / consecutive same-color bars / body width as strength).
data_needed: HA open/high/low/close buffers; optional SMA period (article cites 100-MA in plan); consecutive-color counts.
why_new_for_mis: Averaged-pace candle-color regime sensor that reduces OHLC flicker—cleaner binary trend-state input for MIS than raw candle direction.
quote: Heikin-Ashi charts resemble candlestick charts but have a smoother appearance as they track a range of price movements, rather than tracking every price movement

mechanism: On 8-period RSI: bullish when RSI[0]<RSI[1]<RSI[2]<RSI[3]<20 and RSI[4]>20 (three deepening OS pushes then fourth confirmation after crossing into OS); mirror bearish with >80 and prior bar <80—signals momentum exhaustion / imminent mean-reversion turn (weak in strong trends).
data_needed: RSI period 8, PRICE_CLOSE; last 5 RSI values each bar.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M30 Jan–Jun 2023 demo; multi-symbol Cent-account M30 scan same window
why_new_for_mis: Ordered multi-bar RSI deepening pattern as a change/exhaustion sensor—stricter than single cross of 30/70.
quote: whenever the RSI enters the oversold or overbought level and shapes three consecutive moves deeper while the fourth move being the confirmation (and must be also deeper), then a signal may be given.

mechanism: Collect OHL(+Close target) in MQL5, fit MinMax/Standardization/MeanNorm on independents only, persist mean/min/max/std CSVs; train Keras MLP OHL→Close in Python→ONNX; live path reloads same scaler params before OnnxRun so train and live share identical feature scale—float32 matrices for ONNX compatibility.
data_needed: OPEN/HIGH/LOW(/CLOSE) matrices; saved scaler CSV params; ONNX MLP resource; batch shape [1,3]→[1,1].
why_new_for_mis: Operational neural close-from-OHL sensor with hard train/live normalization lock—MIS can treat scaler-frozen ONNX outputs as comparable sequence features across sessions.
quote: the normalization technique that is used to prepare the training data needs to be the same that is used to prepare the testing and the live data.

mechanism: Detect bullish OB as bearish candle engulfed then ≥2 bullish follow-through (mirror for bearish); zone = that impulse candle’s high–low. Require price revisit into OB and OB aligned with Fib 61.8% of recent swing (bull OB at/below 61.8 from low→high; bear OB at/above 61.8 from high→low) inside a session hour window before entry.
data_needed: OHLC; swing high/low (±5 bars); Fib object; OB rectangle high/low/time; session Time1Hstrt–Time1Hend.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart examples with NY-session hour inputs; backtest equity shown (symbol/TF not uniquely fixed in text)
why_new_for_mis: Liquidity/order-flow zone sensor: institutional OB footprints gated by 61.8% pullback—MIS liquidity-revisit feature beyond plain S/R boxes.
quote: Only if both conditions are met — price within the order block and alignment with the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement — do we proceed to execute a position
